text: dsh-upgrade-guard 是面向 DSH 网页及桌面环境的升级兼容辅助插件。它在设置的通用区域提供操作面板，并通过宿主 webServer 路由调用共享检查引擎。用户可以离线扫描已装插件的已知契约问题、预检插件版本与 DSH 升级兼容情况，并在正式切换前尝试启动新版本进行冒烟验证。扫描覆盖已知服务变化、会话消息契约、宿主导出及精确锁定版本。适合维护 DSH 插件环境、希望在升级前发现兼容问题的用户。预检需要访问 npm registry；其他检查读取本地 profile，不需要 API 密钥。

dsh-upgrade-guard checks DSH plugin compatibility before upgrades. Its settings panel offers an offline contract scan, version preflight, and a boot smoke check on a test port. It suits users maintaining plugin profiles. Preflight accesses npm registry; local checks need no API key.
升级 DSH 前，我想先知道哪些已装插件可能不兼容。
能不能扫描 profile 里插件对宿主服务和导出的引用？
我想比较当前插件版本和升级后可能适用的版本。
更新 DSH 之前怎么列出需要重点检查的插件？
有没有办法先在测试端口启动新版本，确认插件树能正常加载？
Can I check my installed plugins for known DSH contract breaks before upgrading?
I want to compare plugin versions with a planned DSH upgrade.
How can I smoke test a new DSH startup before switching over?
dsh-upgrade-guard 的功能「离线契约扫描」：扫描 profile 中已安装插件，检查已知的服务移除、旧会话 source 结构、宿主 primitives 缺失导出和精确版本锁定，并生成报告。。
dsh-upgrade-guard 的功能「升级前版本预检」：读取 profile 的插件清单并对照目标 DSH 版本及 npm 元数据，整理版本与兼容备注，生成预检报告。。
dsh-upgrade-guard 的功能「启动冒烟检查」：在备用端口启动 DSH 并探测启动输出和页面资源可达性，汇总插件树及启动问题；打包 app.asar 环境不支持此检查。。
dsh-upgrade-guard 的功能「设置面板运行检查」：在设置的通用区域提供契约扫描、联网预检和冒烟检查按钮，并显示结果摘要与宿主信息。。

Stop "upgrading DeepSeek Harness" from turning into "one upgrade, one broken plugin".

[DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) ships fast, and every release can change a contract that plugins depend on. The same class of failure keeps recurring:

text: dsh-upgrade-guard README · dsh-upgrade-guard · upgrade safety net for DeepSeek Harness：This plugin turns the diagnosis of each such incident into a reusable check.
section: dsh-upgrade-guard · upgrade safety net for DeepSeek Harness

text:
dsh-upgrade-guard README · Three actions：| Action | When | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Contract scan** (offline, seconds) | anytime / after upgrading | scans installed plugins against a catalogue of known-breaking contracts: removed service names, old session-message `source` shape, references to `ui-primitives` exports that do not exist |
| **Preflight** (online, 10–40 s) | **before** upgrading | for each plugin: declared compatibility range, newest version on npm, whether it supports the target → "can we upgrade + what must move with it + what to disable" |
| **Boot smoke** (30–90 s) | **before** switching ports | boots a throwaway host on a test port, reads its boot summary (`SKIPPED` / `DEGRADED` / `PENDING` / real culprit), probes each client bundle for reachability, kills the test host afterwards |
dsh-upgrade-guard README · Compatibility (why it works on both web and desktop)：Designed to keep working across 0.1.x and 0.2.x, and on both the web profile and the official desktop app:
section: Compatibility (why it works on both web and desktop)

text:
dsh-upgrade-guard README · Compatibility (why it works on both web and desktop)：- **Zero `@deepseek-ai/*` imports.** The host half imports only Node builtins plus the `webServer` service. The largest historical failure class is "host changed a package/service contract while the plugin still imported the old thing", so this plugin imports none.
- **No hardcoded machine paths.** The profile is found by walking up from the plugin's own location; the host binary/install root is derived from `process.argv[1]`; `ui-primitives` is searched through several candidates. The same files run unchanged in `profiles/web` and `profiles/desktop`.
- **`peerDependencies` declared as `*`, all `optional`.** dsh 0.1.7+ ships a peer-compatibility gate that silently skips bundles declaring a narrow range (e.g. `browser-skill-dsh-plugin@0.3.1` requires `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools: ^0.1.5-rc.3` and gets skipped on 0.2.0-rc.2). A `*` + optional declaration is the declaration shape that survives that gate.

text:
dsh-upgrade-guard README · In the UI：**Settings → General → Upgrade guard** — three buttons plus a footer that tells you which host/runtime/primitives the result came from:

- **Contract scan** → `⚠ critical N / warn N (scanned M plugins)` + findings
- **Preflight** → `📋 target x.y.z: N plugins, K have updates` + the list
- **Boot smoke** → `✅ PASS` / `❌ FAIL` + key output lines (`ROOT?` / `PENDING` / `SKIPPED` / `DEGRADED` / `BADBUNDLE`)

dsh-upgrade-guard README · Command line (same engine)：```powershell
node lib/guard.mjs scan      --json --report scan.md [--profile <dir>] [--primitives <dir>]
node lib/guard.mjs preflight --json --report preflight.md --target 0.1.8-rc.1 [--no-network]
node lib/guard.mjs smoke     --bin <.../dsh/lib/bin.js> --cwd <dir> --port 3099 --timeout 120 [--keep]
```

Environment fallbacks: `DSH_HOME` (default `~/.dsh`), `DSH_PROFILE`, `DSH_PRIMITIVES`, `DSH_SMOKE_BIN`, `DSH_SMOKE_PORT`, `DSH_SMOKE_CWD`, `DSH_SMOKE_TIMEOUT`, `DSH_SMOKE_KEEP=1`.

dsh-upgrade-guard README · Command line (same engine)：Console output is deliberately English/ASCII (Windows `cmd` at code page 936 garbles UTF-8 Chinese); the Chinese report goes to the `--report` file (default `$DSH_HOME/upgrade-guard/`).

dsh-upgrade-guard README · Where the judgement comes from：1. **`removed-service`** — services the host removed or renamed (`settingsScope`, `conversationEvents`, …). Hard references are `critical`; optional `inject([...])` uses are `warn` (the plugin degrades gracefully), and matches inside comments are skipped to avoid false positives.
2. **`session-source-v4`** — the old session-message `source: { kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'x' }` shape (rejected since 0.1.7).
3. **`missing-host-export`** — client code referencing a member absent from the host's `ui-primitives` export table (e.g. the `IconXxx14/16` rename). It only throws `React #130` at render time, so this is a static early warning.
4. **`pinned-exact`** — a plugin pinned to an exact version in the profile (`"x": "1.2.3"`), so it can never follow the host (real case: a plugin pinned and stuck 19 versions behind).
dsh-upgrade-guard README · Where the judgement comes from：**Every new incident adds one rule** — that is the only way this plugin grows, and the reason it gets sharper over time.

dsh-upgrade-guard README · Limits (read these)：- **Smoke only covers boot time**: plugin tree loading, service dependencies, client bundle reachability. **Render-time** errors (e.g. the primitives rename causing `React #130`) will not show up; the contract scan is what covers those.
- **Contract scan only covers the known catalogue.** A brand-new kind of breakage it has never seen stays invisible.
- **Preflight needs npm registry access.** Plugins installed from git/url sources cannot be checked for a newer version and are flagged for manual review.
- **A plugin skipped by the host's peer gate is not a crash** — the host is protecting you. Smoke lists it as `SKIPPED`; reinstalling requires an explicit `dsh plugin allow-version` exemption.
- **Smoke is unavailable in a packaged desktop runtime** (the entry lives inside `app.asar`).

dsh-upgrade-guard README · Layout：```
package.json          dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client declarations
dsh.plugin.json       plugin manifest (name / entry / client)
cordis.patch.yml      the `insert` line that mounts the plugin
lib/index.js          host half: profile+host probing, webServer route, spawns the engine
